params.body:
The two Claude logins (a1, a2) are on a plan that no longer has a five-hour session limit; the weekly limit stays. That session cap used to brake bursts by itself. Without it, one re-tag, a large report import or a bench run can spend an account's week in a day or two. With both accounts refused, every Claude phase stops until the reset, so the signals of the later days are classified and enriched late or not at all, and the Observatory's picture of the week leans towards its first days. This PR paces each account's week evenly and removes the peak-hour brake, which existed only for the session limit.

## On the box

```
SPEND_WEEKLY_USD=350
```

Add this to `.env`. It is per account, in notional list-price dollars. `SPEND_RESERVE_USD` (default a tenth, 35) and `SPEND_BURST_USD` (default half a day's share, 22.50) can stay unset. `SPEND_DAILY_USD` is no longer read and can go.

Optional: `node bin/spend.mjs reset a1 2026-10-08T10:00Z` gives a1 its known weekly reset (Thursday 10:00 UTC) now, instead of after its next refusal. Until an account has a known reset, its week is the rolling last seven days.

## How the figure was found

a1 hit its weekly limit in early October, with its reset on 8 Oct 10:00 UTC, so its week began on 1 Oct 10:00. `/usage?days=30` (a mandated read) starts exactly there:

| | Claude spend, notional |
|---|---|
| Both accounts, 1 Oct 10:00 to 8 Oct 10:00 | $1,121 |
| Both accounts, 1 Oct 10:00 to 4 Oct 10:00 (when the hourly spend falls from $17 to $33 an hour to about $2) | $658 |
| The cohort re-tag dry run in that stretch (phase `classify`, Haiku 4.5) | about $380 |

The re-tag ran as a script, and a script starts on the first configured account, a1. So a1's week held at least the $380 of the re-tag. Adding its half of the workers brings it to about $500.

That read is not split per account, although the rows themselves carry one. So the per-account figure is an estimate, not a measurement. Two more reasons to stay below it:

- **The models changed.** Classify is on Haiku 5.5 and enrich on Sonnet 5 now.
- **The exchange rate may have moved.** A dollar of list price may not weigh the same in the subscription's own measure as it did then.

So the default is 350, below the floor of the estimate. Two accounts at 350 give 630 a week for the background after the reserves, 90 a day. That is about what the pipeline spent on its busiest recent days: $88 on 29 October and $92 on 30 October, Claude only, out of $429 in the last seven days.

After the next weekly refusal, `node bin/spend.mjs` shows what that account's week actually held. Move the figure towards it.

## What changes

**`packages/core/spend.mjs`: a week per account, paced evenly.**
- **The week.** It starts at the account's own weekly reset when one is known. The reset comes from the CLI's refusal ("resets Oct 8, 10am (UTC)"); the last one per account is kept in a new `account_weeks` table. Without a known reset, the week is the rolling last seven days.
- **The background's room.** At any moment the background may have spent (budget − reserve) × the elapsed share of the week, plus a burst allowance. The allowance is at most one day's share. Nothing carries over from last week. In a rolling week there is no elapsed share, so the pace is a day's share plus the allowance in any 24 hours, within the week's total.
- **The fleet.** The hours until the paced room runs out, at the burn of the last three hours, feed the engine's existing throttle ladder. With every account at pace, the paid actions leave the scoring list (classify included) and collect and promote go on.
  - Classify had no budget factor before, so it kept running at the old daily ceiling.
  - Paid actions are now removed from the list, not set to zero, because the worker runs whatever is first in the list, even at score 0.

**Three lanes.**
- **`background`** (the engine, cron phases) is paced. In `accountsToTry`, an account at pace is skipped the way a refused one is, so calls move to the other account. With all accounts at pace, `callCli` throws a paced error: `rateLimited` and `paced`, which is a wait and not a failure.
- **`interactive`**: every request to the server runs in this lane (`withSpendLane` around the handler in `server.mjs`). That covers Ask, the Studio's chat and project setup through `spawnClaudeStream`, and the Studio's other calls. It is never paced; an account at pace is tried last, not skipped. The reserve exists for this lane, so editors are not locked out because the background used the week.
- **`bulk`** (one-off jobs) waits while every account is on or above its even line, checking again every ten minutes. It spends only what the regular flow leaves below the line, and never the allowance or the reserve. Which bulk jobs exist today:
  - `retag-cohort.mjs` and `bin/bench.mjs` declare themselves bulk, and so does `eval-models.mjs`.
  - `SPEND_LANE=bulk` in front of any other command does the same.
  - `enrich-backfill` needs nothing: it only puts signals back in the regular queue.
  - I chose waiting over a separate share because it needs no second number to tune. It also holds by construction: a bulk job can only take what is under the line.

**`packages/engine/supervisor.mjs`: no peak-hour brake.**
- The weekday 13:00 to 19:00 GMT damping is gone: at most two workers, and `expensiveDiscount` × 0.7. Nothing else read the time of day, so it is gone from the state too (`isPeak` is no longer written).
- Each account's headroom now comes from its pace: 100% on or under the even line, falling through the allowance, 0% at pace. An account at pace gets no workers.
- The decision rule moved to `supervisor-decide.mjs`, so the tests run the rule itself instead of a copy.

**Where it shows.**
- `/llm-health` `spend`: the fleet, each account, and the weekly refusals of the last day.
- `/accounts`: each account's `week`.
- The supervisor state: `budget.spend`.
- `/api/elixir` `extra`: `spendWeekUsd`, `spendWeekBudgetUsd`, `spendPaceUsd`, `spendPct`, `spendAheadOfPace`, `spendAtPace`, `spendHoursUntilCeiling` and `spendAccounts`, which replace `spendTodayUsd` and `spendCeilingUsd`.
- `node bin/spend.mjs` prints the same.
- The wall (`/monitor`) gets a "deze week" finding when an account has run ahead of its even line for six hours or more (`aheadOfPaceHoursWeek`), or was refused on its weekly limit in the last day. With every account refused, the finding is "nu".

**CLAUDE.md**: Scoring, Supervisor, Usage Monitoring and Accounts describe the above.

## Tests

- `test/spend.test.mjs` (21 tests):
  - pacing at the start, middle and end of a week, and the burst allowance cap;
  - the reserve, and a known reset against the rolling week;
  - weekly refusals recognised and kept;
  - failover when one account is at pace, and no background account when both are, while interactive keeps both;
  - the bulk lane, the lanes themselves, hours ahead of pace, and the wall's findings.
- `test/supervisor-decide.test.mjs`: the brake's removal (a full queue gets the full ceiling, undamped, with no time of day read), and the pace as headroom.
- `test/engine-sim.test.mjs`: at pace the paid actions leave the list, classify included.
- `test/monitor.test.mjs`: the weekly reading added to the healthy fixture and to the required measurements.

Full suite on the workbench: 1527 of 1533 pass. The 6 failures are all in `report-render` and come from `pdftoppm` not being installed on the workbench (`spawnSync pdftoppm ENOENT`). They are not related to this change.

## Not in this PR

The dashboard's Overview shows a "peak hours" tag when `supervisor.isPeak` is set. Since the field is no longer written, the tag never shows. Removing the dead branch is a separate PR in gentells-dashboard.
params.title: Pace each Claude account's week evenly, and drop the peak-hour brake
